findings.title: Stored XSS: embed URL interpolated unescaped into raw-HTML post
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to the post contents with no HTML/attribute escaping, and the post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`, which (per the new `Post#cook`) bypasses sanitization entirely. The `url` is attacker-influenced: `EmbedController#best` accepts any `embed_url` param and `TopicRetriever` only checks that the URI host equals `embeddable_host`, so the path/query are free-form. `'`, `=`, `(`, `)` are valid URI characters, so a request like `/embed/best?embed_url=http://host/real-post?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` (with a spoofed Referer) makes the job fetch the real page (query strings are ignored by most servers) and store `` in a public topic authored by the embed user. Nokogiri in `absolutize_urls` preserves the injected attribute. Escape `url` with `ERB::Util.html_escape`/`CGI.escapeHTML` (and ideally sanitize the whole imported HTML before storing it as raw_html).

findings.title: Unauthenticated callers can trigger arbitrary server-side fetches and unbounded topic creation
findings.body: Any request to `/embed/best?embed_url=...` with a spoofed `Referer` header (the only check in `ensure_embeddable`) enqueues `RetrieveTopic`, which fetches the URL with `open-uri` and creates a new topic as the `embed_by_username` user. The only constraint is that the URI host matches `embeddable_host`; the path and query string are arbitrary, so `http://host/page?1`, `http://host/page?2`, ... each produce a distinct `TopicEmbed` and topic. The throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed on the full URL (`"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`), so it does not limit this at all. Consequences: unbounded topic spam from the forum's own account, and server-side request amplification (open-uri also follows redirects to any host, so an open redirect on the embeddable site turns this into SSRF). Consider a global rate limit, normalizing/stripping query strings, verifying the fetched page actually references the forum, and/or requiring a successful 200 from a canonical URL.

findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: `absolutize_urls` treats any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` as site-relative and rewrites it to `#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}`. Protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common in feeds and CMS output) also start with `/`, so they are turned into `http://embeddable-host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking every such link and image in imported posts. The same bug is on line 70 for `img[src]`. Check `start_with?('//')` first and only prepend the scheme in that case, or use `URI.join(url, href)` which handles all relative forms correctly.

findings.title: i.content can be nil for RSS items, aborting the whole feed import
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds commonly only provide `description` (and SimpleRSS returns nil for a missing tag), so `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`. Because the loop has no per-item rescue and the job is `retry: false`, a single item without content makes every hourly poll fail and nothing from the feed is ever imported. The same applies to a nil `i.title`. Fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary` and skip items with no usable body instead of raising.

findings.title: Host-spam check still applies to imports and post errors are not checked
findings.body: `PostCreator.new(..., skip_validations: true)` skips model validations but not `rollback_if_host_spam_detected`. Every imported post links to the embeddable host (the appended "Imported from" link plus absolutized links), so once the `embed_by_username` user (typically a fresh TL0 account) has `newuser_spam_host_threshold` (default 3) posts linking that host, `has_host_spam?` returns true, the post is rolled back, and a spam GroupMessage is sent to moderators on every subsequent import. Worse, `PostCreator#create` still returns the unsaved `@post` object, so `if post.present?` is true and `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: post.id)` is attempted with a nil `post_id`, which blows up on the NOT NULL constraint. Check `post.errors.blank?`/`post.persisted?` before creating the embed, and bypass the host-spam check for system imports (or require a trusted import user).

findings.title: Every unknown embed URL triggers a full synchronous feed poll
findings.body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `feed_polling_enabled` is on and the URL has no embed yet. That downloads and parses the entire RSS/Atom feed and runs `TopicEmbed.import` (SHA, Nokogiri parse, possible PostRevisor revision) for every item, before even attempting the direct HTTP fetch. Since the per-URL 60s throttle does not limit distinct URLs, a burst of requests for different (or merely query-string-varied) URLs re-fetches and re-imports the whole feed concurrently from multiple Sidekiq workers, hammering both the remote site and the database. At minimum guard the feed poll with a global short-lived lock/throttle rather than running it per embed URL.

findings.title: SETNX followed by EXPIRE is not atomic; key can become permanent
findings.body: `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` and then a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)`. If the worker dies or the Redis connection fails between the two calls, the key is left with no TTL, and that embed URL is throttled forever (`setnx` will always return false), so its topic can never be retrieved for non-staff users. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (atomic) or wrap in MULTI.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` is a typo that only compiles by accident
findings.body: The conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. Ruby parses the trailing `if` as a statement modifier whose condition is the next generated ERB statement (the buffer append for the following whitespace/text), so the template happens to compile, but the order of evaluation is now dependent on how the ERB engine emits the surrounding code and will break with a syntax error if the following text segment is removed or the template compiler changes (e.g. switching Erubis/Erubi). Replace with `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: `force: true` added to create_table drops existing data on re-run
findings.body: This migration (unrelated to the embed feature) is changed to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, and the new `create_topic_embeds` migration also uses `force: true`. `force: true` issues `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` before creating, so any environment where the table already exists (e.g. re-running migrations after a partial failure, or a schema drift) silently loses all rows. Migrations should not use `force: true`; if the goal is idempotency, guard with `unless table_exists?`.

findings.title: Origin check uses substring match and URL assumes trailing slash
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`. For `discourseUrl = "https://forum.example.com/"`, messages from `https://forum.example.co` or `https://forum.example.c` (any prefix) pass the check, so a different frame on the host page could resize the embed iframe. Compare `e.origin` against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` exactly. Separately, line 7 builds `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`, which produces a broken URL (`...comembed/best`) unless the site owner remembers to include a trailing slash in `discourseUrl`; normalize the base URL.

findings.title: Updating an embed whose post was deleted raises NoMethodError
findings.body: In the update branch, `post = embed.post` uses the `belongs_to :post` association. `Post` includes `Trashable`, whose default scope hides trashed rows, so if a moderator deleted the imported post, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` fails on `@post.raw`. For the hourly `PollFeed` job this exception aborts the import loop for every remaining feed item (and `retry: false`), permanently breaking feed polling once any imported post is deleted. Guard against a nil/trashed post (skip or re-create).

findings.title: Disqus import loses thread created_at/category and may crash on bad links
findings.body: The thread topic was previously created with `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` and an optional `category`; it is now created via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title:)`, which ignores both, so all imported Disqus threads get `created_at = now` (breaking topic ordering/dates) and the `-c` option is silently gone. Also `import_remote` calls `open(url)` before any URL validation: a thread with a missing or relative `link` causes `TypeError`/`Errno::ENOENT` from `Kernel#open` and aborts the whole import rather than being skipped as the `return unless url =~ /^https?:/` guard in `TopicEmbed.import` intends.

findings.title: Core import paths are untested
findings.body: The specs only verify that `execute` delegates to `poll_feed`; `poll_feed` itself (SimpleRSS parsing, the `i.content` nil case, link/id fallback), `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` (protocol-relative and non-standard-port cases), and the escaping of the appended "Imported from" link are all without coverage. In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` the example titled "is 404 without an embed_url" actually exercises `params.require`, which raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (HTTP 400), and the assertion is only `should_not be_success`, so the title is misleading and would not catch a regression in the status code.
